chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

A man came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, a boy was born to me, so what should I name him?' He said: 'Name him with the name most dear to me: Hamzah.'

key_terms.صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ: Peace be upon him and his family

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended practice for naming a newborn boy according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the Prophet’s preference for 'Hamzah', the name of his beloved uncle and a symbol of early Islamic valor, thereby elevating it as a virtuous choice for newborns. In Shia scholarly tradition, this narration underscores the significance of honoring the Ahl al-Bayt and their close companions through naming practices, linking personal identity to spiritual lineage. It serves as a practical guideline for Muslims to select names that reflect piety and connection to prophetic heritage.
